players.product: High-complexity multilayer PCBs, substrates and advanced packaging for AI data-center/networking systems

quarterly_data.signal: First-ever $1 billion quarter: Q2 net sales of $1.0 billion, up 37% year over year from $731 million, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.99 per diluted share, up 71% - both all-time highs and both above guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $166.8 million or 16.6% of sales, up 160 basis points year over year and 90 basis points sequentially on favourable mix. Non-GAAP gross margin was 21.9% (+100bps) and operating margin 13.8% (+270bps) on volume, mix and SG&A discipline. GAAP operating income was $109.1 million and GAAP EPS $0.77. Management reiterated that roughly 80% of net sales are tied to the AI and defense megatrends.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 sales $1.0B (+37% YoY); non-GAAP EPS $0.99 (+71%); adjusted EBITDA $166.8M (16.6%, +160bps YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: net sales of $1.10-1.14 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.21-1.27, with a further sequential uptick expected in Q4. Full-year 2026 is now guided to approximately $4.4 billion of sales with non-GAAP EPS approaching $5 - both excluding any contribution from the pending European acquisitions - versus the previously communicated plan of at least $4 billion. Management reaffirmed confidence in 15% to 20% ORGANIC revenue growth for both 2027 and 2028, with further clarity promised next quarter alongside an updated long-term plan. Q3 assumes ~107.7 million diluted shares, SG&A ~7% of sales, R&D ~1%, and a 13-17% tax rate.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $1.10B-$1.14B, EPS $1.21-$1.27; FY2026 ~$4.4B sales, EPS approaching $5; 15-20% organic growth reaffirmed for 2027-2028

quarterly_data.signal: Data center and networking was 40% of Q2 sales and grew 91% year over year, above expectations, on AI data-center build-out demand. It is guided to 49% of net sales in Q3 as the N+M ramp begins, and full-year 2026 sales in the end market are now expected to MORE THAN DOUBLE year over year. On customer concentration, TTM has one 10% customer in commercial and one in aerospace and defense, with another commercial customer approaching 10%; management described the commercial roster as 'getting a bit crowded,' with 10-plus large hyperscaler and networking companies in the field.
quarterly_data.figure: Data center & networking 40% of Q2 sales, +91% YoY; guided to 49% of Q3 sales; FY2026 to more than double

quarterly_data.signal: N+M asymmetrical interconnect printed circuit boards entered the early stage of full production launch. TTM has already delivered 'tens of millions' with yields running better than planned, and about $600 MILLION of N+M is scheduled for the second half of 2026 - roughly one third in Q3 and two thirds in Q4 - with adjusted EBITDA margins improving as the yield curve improves. CEO Edwin Roks stressed N+M is 'not just one process, it's a family of different options' and only the first step, supporting multiple customers beyond data center and networking. Asked whether an incremental $1 billion of N+M revenue in 2027 was the right figure, Roks said it 'could be in the ballpark,' with the precise number pending the bottom-up annual plan.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$600M of N+M in H2 2026 (1/3 Q3, 2/3 Q4); 2027 incremental N+M 'could be in the ballpark' of $1B

quarterly_data.signal: Order book at record levels: overall book-to-bill was 1.49 in Q2 (commercial segment 1.63, aerospace and defense 1.3). The 90-day backlog, which is subject to cancellation, was $901 million versus $497 million a year ago - an 81% increase. The aerospace and defense total program backlog rose to $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion a year ago, and qualified business proposals in the A&D strategic pipeline are at an all-time high of over $7 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: Book-to-bill 1.49 (commercial 1.63, A&D 1.3); 90-day backlog $901M (+81% YoY); A&D program backlog $1.7B; >$7B qualified A&D pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: Laminate material supply is tightening at the low end, not the high end. CCL (copper-clad laminate) producers are shifting away from lower-complexity materials toward higher-complexity products, which puts slight pressure on material availability - felt in automotive and other lower-end parts of the portfolio rather than in the high-end data center materials such as T-glass. Management said lead times remain decent, high-end materials are available, customers are not suffering, and TTM is actively working with supply chain partners to secure supply in line with customer demand. Automotive is guided to about 6% of Q3 sales partly because of this dynamic.

Capacity build-out: the new Syracuse facility begins initial volume ramp of Ultra-HDI products in Q3, continuing through Q4 and 2027 to reach full capacity run rate in 2028. Penang is at 'very decent revenue levels' and close to breakeven, expected late Q3 or Q4; it now runs N+M - one of the most difficult technologies in the company - and supports some data center and networking customers alongside its core medical/instrumentation/industrial base. The Wisconsin (Eau Claire) site, bought for less than $20 million, will host some production plus an innovation center near Chippewa Falls, deliberately unrushed. Growth capacity is coming mainly from brownfield expansion of existing sites, particularly in China, and the board approved accelerated capital expenditure that raises the full-year 2026 capex range by around $45 million at both ends.
quarterly_data.figure: Syracuse Ultra-HDI full run rate 2028; Penang breakeven late Q3/Q4; FY2026 capex range raised ~$45M

quarterly_data.signal: Aerospace and defense was 37% of Q2 sales and grew 14% year over year on defense budget tailwinds and program alignment. Q2 bookings included the APS-153 multi-mode maritime surveillance radar, the ATP Sensor System for targeting and surveillance, Golden Dome and a number of restricted priority programs. The segment is guided to about 32% of Q3 sales with continued year-on-year and sequential growth, and full-year 2026 growth in the low to mid teens. The business splits between Ultra-HDI PCBs and 'up-the-chain' RF modules, subsystems and complete radar systems, both performing well.
quarterly_data.figure: A&D 37% of Q2 sales, +14% YoY; guided ~32% of Q3 sales; FY2026 growth low-to-mid teens

quarterly_data.signal: TTM announced its intention to acquire two privately held European companies - Swiss Technology Group AG (STG) in Switzerland and ILFA GmbH in Germany - with the transaction expected to close in Q3 2026 pending regulatory clearance. Together they represent less than 5% of incremental sales and are expected to be moderately accretive on an adjusted EBITDA basis, establishing TTM's first European footprint in long-cycle medical and A&D businesses. Q2 GAAP results included a $14 million non-cash pretax unrealized loss from a deal-contingent cross-currency swap hedging the Swiss-franc purchase price, which could not receive hedge accounting because the deal had not closed.
quarterly_data.figure: STG + ILFA: <5% incremental sales, closing Q3 2026; $14M non-cash swap loss in Q2 GAAP results

quarterly_data.signal: Medical, industrial and instrumentation grew 33% year over year, helped by healthy medical demand including major continuous glucose monitoring products and by instrumentation for AUTOMATED TEST EQUIPMENT SUPPORTING AI SOLUTIONS. Year to date the top five medical customers have more than doubled internal expectations, with further growth expected from surgical robots, electrophysiology and continuous glucose measurement. The end market is guided to 13% of Q3 sales and full-year 2026 growth of 35% to 40%. Automotive was 8% of Q2 sales and marginally down year over year, with full-year sales still expected to decline mid single digits as TTM stays selective on higher-value work.
quarterly_data.figure: MI&I +33% YoY, FY2026 growth 35-40%, guided to 13% of Q3 sales; automotive 8% of Q2 sales, FY2026 down mid-single digits

quarterly_data.signal: Cash flow from operating activities was $96.4 million in Q2 (versus $97.8 million a year ago) and free cash flow was $46.0 million (versus $37.6 million). Net leverage stands at a healthy 0.9x. Interest expense was $9.9 million and interest income $1.9 million; a weaker U.S. dollar produced a $4.9 million foreign exchange loss. The effective tax rate was 15.0%, giving tax expense of $18.9 million.
